name: LM2841XBMKX_NOPB
title: Buck regulator, 4.5 V to 42 V input, 100 mA, 300 mA or 600 mA output, thin SOT-23-6
summary: LM2840, LM2841 and LM2842 are non-synchronous buck regulators with an internal 0.9 Ω switch, running from 4.5 V to 42 V and rated for 100 mA, 300 mA and 600 mA of load. Each comes at a fixed 550 kHz (X) or 1.25 MHz (Y). The output is set by a divider to a 0.765 V feedback reference; compensation is internal, and soft start is set by an RC on the SHDN pin. Thermal shutdown, input and gate-drive undervoltage lockout and current limit are built in; shutdown current is 16 µA typical.

0.9 Ω typ, 1.6 Ω max over TJ
1.35 mA typ, on, no load; 16 µA typ in shutdown

pins.name: CB
pins.function: Gate-drive supply for the internal switch. A capacitor, CBOOT, goes from CB to SW.

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input. The tap of a divider from the output sets VOUT = VFB × (1 + R1 / R2); keep the resistors between 100 Ω and 10 kΩ so the bias current does not add error.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Active-low logic shutdown: low disables the regulator, high enables it. Tie to VIN when not used; never leave it open.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input, 4.5 V to 42 V in normal operation.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Output of the internal power switch. The inductor, the rectifier diode and CBOOT all join this pin.

circuits.title: 3.3 V output at 100 mA (Figure 9)
circuits.description: A step-down regulator taking 4.5 V to 42 V down to 3.3 V for a 100 mA load. SHDN is strapped to VIN so the regulator runs whenever input is present. CBOOT between CB and SW lifts the gate drive of the internal high-side switch above the input. When the switch opens, Schottky D1 carries the inductor current from ground. R1 from the output and R2 to ground divide VOUT down to the 0.765 V feedback reference at FB. CIN is the ceramic input bypass and COUT the output filter.
notes: Design parameters: 4.5 V to 42 V in, 3.3 V out, 0.1 A.

operation.text: LM2840, LM2841 and LM2842 differ in rated load: 100 mA, 300 mA and 600 mA. The letter after the number picks the oscillator: X runs at 550 kHz, Y at 1.25 MHz. All three are adjustable, with a 0.765 V nominal feedback voltage, and come in the 6-pin thin SOT-23 (DDC). Automotive Q1 versions (LM2840-Q1, LM2841-Q1, LM2842-Q1) exist as separate devices.

A non-synchronous, current-mode PWM buck converter with an internal power MOSFET between VIN and SW and internal loop compensation. The oscillator, an error amplifier against a bandgap reference with soft start, a PWM comparator, a current-limit block measuring inductor current, a maximum duty-cycle limit, thermal shutdown and a UVLO comparator drive the FET driver. The gate driver runs from the CB pin, which takes a bootstrap capacitor to SW; the rectifier diode is external.

While the inductor current stays above zero, each cycle has two phases. With the switch on, the diode is reverse biased and the inductor current rises, feeding the load and charging the inductor. With the switch off, the inductor current keeps flowing through the now forward-biased diode, into COUT and the load. The on-to-off ratio sets the output voltage.

Thermal shutdown turns the power switch off when the die gets too hot (175°C typical trip, 155°C typical release). Input undervoltage lockout keeps the part off below the minimum input voltage during power-up and power-down (3.7 V typical on, 3.5 V typical off). A second lockout on the CB gate-drive supply stops switching until there is enough gate voltage for the MOSFET. The switch current is limited cycle by cycle, and the output is short-circuit protected.

SHDN is a logic-level enable: low turns the part off, cutting the supply current to about 16 µA, and 2.3 V or more turns it on. When unused, tie SHDN to VIN; it must never float. The voltage on SHDN should stay below 42 V; a higher control voltage can be used through a series resistor of 100 kΩ or more.

Between 0 V and 2.3 V on SHDN, the per-cycle current limit scales with the pin voltage, from its minimum at 0 V up to the full rated limit at 2.3 V. An RC network on SHDN therefore ramps the current limit at start-up, which sets the output rise time and limits inrush. The resistor must supply more than the 1.5 µA SHDN leakage once the pin is at 2.3 V or above.

Inductance, peak current rating and DC resistance matter most. Size the inductance for a ripple current of about 30 % of the DC output current, at the highest input voltage since ripple grows with VIN. More ripple means smaller inductance but more conduction and core loss, more stress on the switch and inductor, and a bigger COUT to hold the same ripple. Letting the copper loss be about 2 % of output power balances efficiency against size. 10 µH to 22 µH is a starting point, rated 1.1 A or more for the LM2842 and 0.7 A or more for the others, so the part reaches current limit before the inductor saturates under a short or long overload.

A low-ESR ceramic capacitor of 2.2 µF to 10 µF, X5R or X7R, from VIN to GND holds down input transients. Ceramic capacitors can lose up to 50 % of their capacitance at rated voltage, so allow for voltage and temperature derating.

COUT is chosen for the allowed output ripple, which is usually set mostly by the capacitor's ESR. Ceramic parts with low ESR are the recommended type; 22 µF to 100 µF with ESR of 0.1 Ω or less is a starting range.
CBOOT should be a ceramic capacitor of 0.15 µF or more. Where VIN is less than twice VOUT, use a larger one, 0.15 µF to 1 µF, to keep the gate drive strong and RDSON low.

Choose a reverse voltage rating about 25 % above the highest input voltage and a current rating matching the largest output current. At duty cycles above 50 % the average diode current drops to about (1 − D) × IOUT and a lower average rating can be used, but its peak rating should still be above the largest load current. Start from a diode rated 0.5 A to 1 A.
R2 is typically 100 Ω to 10 kΩ; keeping the divider resistors in the 100 Ω to 10 kΩ range keeps the FB bias current from shifting the output.

The supply range for the part is 4 V to 42 V. The source must deliver the peak input current and stay above 4.5 V. Its impedance has to be small enough that a step in input current cannot drag VIN down into a UVLO trip. A source more than a few inches away may need bulk capacitance added beside the ceramic input capacitors.

Return the feedback divider's ground leg straight to the GND pin on its own trace, and keep R1 and R2 near FB and away from the inductor. Put CIN close to VIN to keep input ripple down. Put L1 close to SW to limit EMI and capacitive coupling. Put COUT close to where L1 and D1 meet, and keep the L1, D1 and COUT loop as short as possible. Keep the ground connections of D1, CIN and COUT small and join them to the ground plane at a single point, preferably at the COUT ground.
